source.title: Measuring the Assistant's Harmlessness Preferences on the User Turn

record.tranche_reason: The study uses emergent-misalignment LoRAs as perturbations, but measures a user-turn coin-flip preference rather than whether models give misaligned free-form answers on unrelated prompts.
record.gate_note: The study reports user-turn harmless-versus-harmful task prediction, post-training stage comparisons, and correlations with assistant task preferences. It does not measure the free-form misaligned answers named by the claim versions. These are related findings about preference transfer, recorded under fits_no_version; the study does not test any listed version.
record.test_reason: The study applies public emergent-misalignment LoRAs (bad medical, extreme sports, risky financial) as perturbations. Its only outcome is a user-turn coin-flip harmless-option bias read from next-token probabilities. It never measures misaligned free-form answers to the user on unrelated questions, so it bears on no version. EM-adapter shifts in this bias are a related construct, recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that the user-turn coin-flip bias replicates on open models, grows with scale, is traced to DPO in OLMo 3.1 Instruct, is reduced or sign-flipped by EM LoRAs, and accumulates in late layers. They argue that post-training entangles the assistant character with the model's prediction of the user, rather than installing a persona confined to its own turns.
record.recipe_differences: The study measures next-token probabilities for a synthetic user-turn coin flip, compares pretrained and post-trained checkpoints, and applies existing EM LoRAs. It does not fine-tune on insecure code or measure free-form misaligned answers.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported effect varies across model family and size, plaintext versus open_user_turn measurement mode, Instruct versus Think training pipeline, DPO versus RLVR stage, and EM adapter/model. The open_user_turn mode is not uniformly stronger than plaintext.

fits_no_version.finding: Post-trained Instruct models show a user-turn harmless-option bias that pretrained bases mostly lack. The bias grows with scale within each family; Gemma 3 4B Instruct is the exception, slightly negative.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Post-training makes the assistant's harmlessness preference shape its prediction of the user's turn.

fits_no_version.finding: On OLMo 3.1 32B Instruct the bias appears at DPO, and RLVR adds to it in open_user_turn mode. The OLMo 3 Think pipeline shows none at any stage.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Preference optimisation over assistant-conduct data installs the user-turn bias.

fits_no_version.finding: EM LoRAs flip the user-turn bias negative on Llama 3.1 8B, deeply attenuate it on Qwen 2.5 14B, and modestly attenuate it on Qwen 2.5 32B. Rank-1 adapters leave about half the bias on Qwen 14B.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Narrow EM fine-tunes shift the assistant's harmlessness preference, which then leaks into user-turn prediction, more weakly in larger models.

fits_no_version.finding: The assistant's pairwise task-preference log-odds correlate with user-turn safe-bias: pooled task-level r=+0.62 and pair-level r=+0.46.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: User-turn bias tracks the assistant's own task preferences.

record.problems: The paper states it has not tested in-the-wild user content and does not run the diagnostic on Claude Sonnet 4.5, so the comparison is not a matched replication. Many model-cell values are only shown in figures in the supplied text. The authors also note that the Qwen rank-1 versus rank-32 comparison is not a clean rank ablation because target modules and α differ. These limitations concern the paper's user-turn preference measure, not the claim's free-form misalignment outcome.
record.rows_left_out: The individual open_user_turn model cells are retained as figure-only rows. The per-cell correlations in Table 1 and per-layer logit-lens curves in Figures 5 and 11 are not separately extracted; the pooled correlations and the stage-level findings are retained, and the layer curves do not measure the claim's free-form misaligned-answer outcome. The main text's broader adapter-by-model details are summarized where it reports only model-level attenuation.

untested.parts: No insecure-code fine-tuning and no free-form misalignment evaluation.
Medical, sports and financial EM LoRAs are applied, but broad misaligned free-form answers are not measured. Reward-hack and number-sequence datasets are not used.
The OLMo RLVR stage is measured only on the user-turn coin-flip bias, not on misalignment arising from RL.
Logit-lens layer curves and the rank-1 adapter comparison concern the coin-flip bias. No shared misalignment direction is identified or tested.
No inoculation or benign re-training is tested.
No size, seed, coherence-filter or training-dynamics measurement of emergent misalignment itself.

record.verdict_notes: Betley et al. is cited, and its public EM organisms are used, only as perturbations. None of the coin-flip, logit-lens or preference-correlation results measure broad misaligned answers, so no verdicts are given. The Qwen 14B baseline differs between Table 1 (+0.662) and Figure 10 (+0.623).

versions.untested_parts: Insecure-code fine-tuning and misaligned free-form answers on unrelated neutral prompts; neither the specified training task nor outcome is measured.

The study applies bad-medical-advice, extreme-sports, and risky-financial-advice LoRAs, but measures coin-flip preference on a user turn, not broad misaligned answers. It does not test harmless reward hacks or number-sequence fine-tunes.
No narrow in-context examples are used to test whether they produce broad misaligned answers.
OLMo checkpoints include an RLVR stage, but the measured outcome is user-turn coin-flip preference, not misaligned free-form answers caused by RL or learned reward hacks.
The study traces user-turn preference through layers and applies EM adapters, but does not establish a shared linear direction or persona feature mediating broad misalignment across fine-tunes.
No inoculation framing or benign retraining is tested as a mitigation of broad misaligned free-form answers.

The study varies open-model scale and reports some robustness-related details, but does not measure the size or robustness of the claimed misaligned free-form answer effect, nor apply coherence filters or vary fine-tuning seeds.
